Tune every channel's carryover jointly, inside one model

Source: R/tune-carryover-joint.R
tune_carryover_joint.Rd

The multi-channel counterpart of tune_carryover(). Each channel's (max_lag, decay) is chosen by forward-only cross-validation of a model containing all the channels and any control variables, so a channel's carryover is judged with the others' effects accounted for rather than absorbed.

Usage

tune_carryover_joint(
  media,
  y,
  controls = NULL,
  fit_fn = NULL,
  predict_fn = NULL,
  max_lags = Inf,
  decays = seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.05),
  normalise = TRUE,
  scheme = c("rolling_origin", "k_fold_forward"),
  metric_fn = rmse,
  initial = NULL,
  assess = 1L,
  skip = 0L,
  k = 5L,
  aggregate = c("pooled", "mean"),
  start = NULL,
  max_iter = 10L,
  warm_start = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  by = NULL,
  index = NULL,
  se_block = 1L,
  save_pred = FALSE
)

Arguments

media

A data frame (or matrix with column names) of raw media, one column per channel, rows in time order unless index is given. Every column must be finite and must vary.

y

Numeric vector of the KPI, one value per row of media.

controls

Optional data frame of control variables, such as trend, price, seasonality and holidays, entered into the model untransformed. Character, factor and logical columns are expanded to treatment dummies by stats::model.matrix() and every name is made syntactic. A column with a single value is dropped with a message, and missing or non-finite values are an error that names the column and rows. No control may share a name with a channel.

fit_fn, predict_fn

Optional model. fit_fn(X, y) receives a data frame of the adstocked media followed by the controls; predict_fn(model, X) returns predictions for new rows of the same shape. Leaving both NULL (the default) fits ordinary least squares with an intercept; giving only one is an error.

max_lags, decays

Candidate kernel lengths and decays, shared by every channel. See tune_carryover().

normalise

Should the adstock kernel be normalised to sum to 1? See adstock_geometric().

scheme

Resampling scheme. "rolling_origin" (the default) grows the training window one step at a time and assesses on the periods immediately following. "k_fold_forward" splits the periods after the first training window into k contiguous blocks and assesses each with a model trained on every period before it. Both are forward-only; neither ever trains on data that follows what it assesses.

metric_fn

A function of (actual, predicted) returning a single number to be minimised. Defaults to rmse().

initial

Size of the first training window, in periods. Defaults to half the series for scheme = "rolling_origin", and to floor(n / (k + 1)) for scheme = "k_fold_forward", in both cases rounded down.

assess

Number of periods assessed per split. Used by scheme = "rolling_origin" only; the forward-block scheme's assessment sizes are determined by k and the series length.

skip

Number of splits to skip between evaluations, to make a long series cheaper. 0 evaluates every split. Used by scheme = "rolling_origin" only.

k

Number of forward blocks when scheme = "k_fold_forward". Ignored otherwise.

aggregate

How to turn the assessment sets into one score. "pooled" (the default) collects every out-of-sample prediction across splits and evaluates metric_fn once on the lot, so rmse really is the root mean squared forecast error. "mean" evaluates metric_fn on each split and averages, which is the tune convention. With assess = 1 a per-split RMSE is an absolute error, so the mean of them is a mean absolute error whatever metric_fn is called.

start

Optional numeric vector of starting decays in [0, 1], named by channel. Each channel it names starts at the grid point with the nearest decay; the others start, as every channel does by default, at the middle of decays.

max_iter

Maximum number of full sweeps over the channels.

warm_start

Seed each adstocked series with adstock_steady_state() instead of starting from zero, removing the start-up bias of long-carryover channels. As in tune_carryover(), the seed uses no media from beyond the first training window.

cores

Number of cores over which each channel's grid points are scored. Values above 1 use parallel::mclapply() on Unix-alikes and a socket cluster elsewhere. The workers of a socket cluster are new R sessions that load mediamix and nothing else, so there fit_fn and predict_fn must call other packages with pkg::fun() and must not rely on functions or data defined in your session. metric_fn runs in your session.

by, index

Panel data, as in tune_carryover(). by assigns each row to a series, as a vector or a data frame of key columns, and index gives each row's period, as a number, Date or POSIXct. With index the rows may come in any order. by needs index. Every channel is adstocked within each series; see Panel data in tune_carryover().

se_block

Number of consecutive splits the jackknife leaves out together when it computes std_err and the one-standard-error rule. 1, the default, treats the splits as independent. Successive forecasts share most of their training data, so their errors are usually correlated and independence understates the standard error; a block of a few splits allows for that. best does not depend on it.

save_pred

Keep the out-of-sample predictions of the selected values? FALSE by default, as in tune's control_resamples(). With TRUE the result gains predictions, for best and for the best_1se set. The other grid points' predictions are not kept: each channel's final profile alone holds one set per grid point, so keeping them would need a row for every channel, grid point and assessed row.

Value

An object of class mm_carryover_joint: a list with

best

One row per channel: channel, max_lag, decay, half_life.

best_1se

The same, with each channel's value chosen by the paired one-standard-error rule on its own final profile, anchored on its value in best. See The one-standard-error set.

best_1se_metric

The cross-validated metric of the best_1se values taken together.

profiles

Each channel's cross-validation profile from the final sweep, with the other channels held at their selected values: channel, max_lag, decay, half_life, metric, std_err.

metric

The cross-validated metric at the selected values, scored on the n_ok splits that the best and best_1se sets both completed.

metric_name

Name of the metric function used.

iterations, converged

Sweeps run, and whether the last sweep changed nothing.

predictions

Only with save_pred = TRUE: the forecasts of best and of the best_1se set on the splits both completed, one row per set per assessed row. Columns: selection ("best" or "best_1se"), split (the split's position among the n_splits formed), row (the row of media and y), index and group (with index and by), max_lag_<channel> and decay_<channel> for each channel, observed and predicted. When the two sets are the same, the best_1se rows repeat the best rows.

plus scheme, aggregate, n_splits, n_ok, n_series and normalise, as in tune_carryover(), except that n_ok counts the splits the two selected sets completed rather than every grid point. Each channel's profile is compared on the splits its own grid completed, which can be fewer. as.data.frame() and tidy() return profiles with logical columns best and best_1se marking each channel's selections.

Details

The search is coordinate descent: each sweep visits the channels in turn and sets each one to its best grid point with the others held fixed, repeating until a sweep changes nothing. Each step can only lower the cross-validated error, so the search terminates, but like any coordinate method it finds a local optimum of the grid, not necessarily the global one. A different start is a cheap check. The cost is roughly channels x grid size x sweeps cross-validated fits, far fewer than the full grid's grid size ^ channels; cores spreads each channel's grid points over several processes.

A grid point whose fit fails on some splits is handled as in tune_carryover(): within each step every grid point is scored on the splits all of them completed. A warning reports the most splits any step left out, and a selection on the edge of the grid is reported for each channel.

Saturation is not tuned here. For carryover, saturation and a model penalty tuned jointly, use step_adstock() and step_saturation() with tune; see vignette("tidymodels").

The one-standard-error set

Each channel's one-standard-error choice is made on its own profile, with the other channels held at best, so the rule is applied channel by channel. Shortening several channels at once can cost more than any one of them does alone, and the combination was not part of the search. The set is therefore scored as a whole after the search, and best_1se_metric reports that score next to metric. When the gap between the two is large against the profiles' std_err, the channels' near-ties do not add up to a near-tie for the set, and best_1se is better read one channel at a time.

See also

tune_carryover() for one channel, plot_carryover() for the profiles, adstock_steady_state()

Examples

data(mm_weekly)
north <- mm_weekly[mm_weekly$geo == "north", ]
channels <- c("tv", "video", "search", "social", "display")
controls <- data.frame(week = seq_len(nrow(north)), price = north$price,
                       seasonality = north$seasonality,
                       holiday = north$holiday)

joint <- tune_carryover_joint(north[channels], north$revenue,
                              controls = controls,
                              decays = seq(0.05, 0.95, by = 0.1),
                              skip = 3, save_pred = TRUE)
#> Warning: The chosen parameters sit on the edge of the grid.
#> • display: the selected decay (0.95) is the largest value searched.
#> ℹ Widen the grid and re-run. A parameter pinned to a boundary usually means the
#>   optimum is outside it, or that the series is too short to identify carryover
#>   this long.
joint
#> 
#> ── Joint carryover tuning 
#> 5 channels, rolling_origin resampling, 20 splits; 3 sweeps, converged
#> rmse (pooled) = 788.545
#> One-SE set, chosen channel by channel: rmse = 867.986
#>  channel max_lag decay half_life decay_1se
#>       tv     Inf  0.85     4.265      0.85
#>    video     Inf  0.45     0.868      0.05
#>   search     Inf  0.75     2.409      0.05
#>   social     Inf  0.65     1.609      0.25
#>  display     Inf  0.95    13.513      0.45
#> 40 out-of-sample predictions kept in `$predictions`.
rbind(truth = attr(mm_weekly, "truth")$decay[channels],
      joint = joint$best$decay)
#>         tv video search social display
#> truth 0.85  0.70   0.15   0.45    0.55
#> joint 0.85  0.45   0.75   0.65    0.95

# The selected values' forecasts of the weeks each split held out
kept <- joint$predictions[joint$predictions$selection == "best", ]
head(kept[c("split", "row", "observed", "predicted")])
#>   split row observed predicted
#> 1     1  79    29396  29986.39
#> 2     2  83    24098  22656.69
#> 3     3  87    17509  17744.49
#> 4     4  91    23845  23695.48
#> 5     5  95    20278  20235.17
#> 6     6  99    21398  22520.96
